ratings_why.fun: Lots of stacking: Barley-Sugar Twiner plus Viscum doubles a gain twice, Ivy of the Grand Oak plus Traveller's Joy loops stats front and back, and every turn asks where to stand.
ratings_why.distinct: Over a 7 because no tribe today has a payoff that is another tribe's carry, and the staggered back row (each slot picking between two hosts) makes board layout the main decision.

verdict_why: The rules read cleanly now and the combos are rich; more passes would likely change it, not improve it.

points.text: Barley-Sugar Twiner and Viscum on one host is the best combo here: the repeat is a new gain, so Viscum copies both in full. Say so in build A so players find it.
Ivy of the Grand Oak's Start of Combat gain is a fight gain, so Traveller's Joy sends half of it back to every climber. Worth stating the order so it reads as a deliberate payoff.
Kissing Bough is the one card with no decision: picking a berry is flavour. Let a berry go to any host, or let you save berries for a big turn.
Blackcap giving Climb to a front-row unit does nothing until Ivy-clad Ruin. A line pointing at that pairing, or at grafting Climb onto Cousin Dodder in the back, would show its off-label uses.
Hosts can also be climbers once Ruin is out, so one unit can feed and be fed. That cross-wiring is where this tribe shines; one more card that rewards it would push it further.

standouts.why: Copies every gain in full but loses his host if he outgrows it, so you manage the gap every turn.
Turns Apple Mistletoe, Grand Oak and Cousin Dodder fight gains into back-row stats; the glue card of the parasite build.
Pushes you to rotate her behind hosts of new tribes, a real puzzle each turn in a mixed board.

weakest.why: Four flat buffs and a sell; no choice in it.
Plain gold for buying the host's tribe; useful but does one obvious job.
A vanilla early body with a small fight drain; nothing to combo with.

flags.note: Viscum plus one or two Twiners on an Ooze or Cousin Dodder carry multiplies huge single gains; Viscum's biggest-unit rule is the only brake.
At five signatures every host gains +10/+10 a turn, each echoed by its climbers; strong in a five-tribe lobby.
